decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add… bookmarks.” Round 1 client refers to the add-bookmark flow and entering/pasting a link.
decisions.note: The recorded save-by-URL behavior conforms at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only says “edit… bookmarks”; neither presentation specifies whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable. The client’s later general approval does not clarify these fields.
decisions.note: The generic editing claim is insufficient to establish conformity or divergence; final approval does not resolve it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add, edit, delete… bookmarks.” Round 1 client says the rest is close to what was intended.
decisions.note: Deleting bookmarks directly conforms at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only “Search with ⌘/Ctrl + K”; no searchable fields, case behavior, tag syntax, boolean operators, parentheses, or phrase semantics are described. The client merely acknowledges “searching.”
decisions.note: The presented search decision lacks enough semantics to determine divergence; bare approval does not resolve it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “Collections,” and the client acknowledges collections, but the transcript does not establish whether these permit multi-tag assignment/filtering or are dynamic saved filters with included/excluded tags and a search term.
decisions.note: The categorization behavior may be equivalent to tags or bundles, but the evidence cannot establish that; it remains unresolved rather than being treated as divergent.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Sorting by date or title.” Round 1 client acknowledges that the app handles sorting.
decisions.note: Offering date and title sort keys conforms at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client observes the presented behavior: “I have to type in the title and description myself” and requests the replacement behavior: “I paste in a link, and the app goes and fetches the page's title, description, and icon for me automatically.” Round 2 maker calls this an implemented addition.
decisions.note: At the initial implementation review, manual metadata entry diverged from automatic collection; the client supplied the reference-aligned behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client: “the little colored squares are just initials rather than the actual site icons” and asks for the page icon to be fetched. Round 2 client confirms “the real site icon.”
decisions.note: At the initial implementation review, initials replaced the required per-item favicon; the client explicitly corrected this.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests the missing capability: “mark a bookmark as ‘to read.’” Round 2 maker says this was one of “both additions” and that items can be returned to the queue.
decisions.note: The initial scope omitted an unread/read-later state; the client extended it with the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests to “see just those unread ones on their own.” Round 2 maker adds “a dedicated reading queue.”
decisions.note: The initial implementation lacked the separate unread view; the client requested it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client asks to “check them off once I've read them.” Round 2 maker adds one-click marking as read.
decisions.note: The initial implementation lacked the transition that removes read items from the unread list; the client requested it.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker’s revised fetch list is “title, description, final URL, and favicon,” omitting the required preview image. Round 2 client praises title, description, and icon and says “exactly what I was hoping for,” without mentioning the preview-image difference.
decisions.note: This revised implementation decision remains partial because preview-image collection is absent. The client’s approval does not express awareness of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker already presents bookmark editing; Round 2 maker says metadata fields “remain editable,” and the client confirms “I can still fix anything it doesn't get.”
decisions.note: Across the revised implementation review, collected title/description remain user-editable, conforming to the recorded requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says the favicon is fetched; Round 2 client verifies that saving now shows “the real site icon.”
decisions.note: The revised implementation records conforming favicon exposure.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “New bookmarks default to ‘To read’” and bookmarks can be “returned to the queue in one click.” Round 2 client confirms the behavior matches the intended reading workflow.
decisions.note: The revised implementation supports assigning unread status.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Added a dedicated reading queue with live counts.” Round 2 client confirms the “‘To read’ queue with the count.”
decisions.note: The revised implementation provides the conforming separate unread view.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Bookmarks can be marked read… in one click.” Round 2 client confirms being able to “mark something read.”
decisions.note: The revised implementation provides the conforming mark-read action.
